chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Zureys Al-Kunasi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a woman and a slave who killed a man by error. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The error of the woman and the slave is like the deliberate. So if the guardians of the slain wish to kill both of them, they kill both of them. If the value of the slave is more than five thousand dirhams, let them return to the master of the slave what remains after the five thousand dirhams. And if they wish to kill the woman and take the slave, they take him, unless his value is more than five thousand dirhams, in which case let them return to the master of the slave what remains after the five thousand dirhams, and take the slave, or his master ransoms him. And if the value of the slave is less than five thousand dirhams, they have nothing except the slave.'
ai.seo_question: What are the rules for blood money and compensation when a woman and a slave kill someone accidentally?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the legal principle of 'kaffarah' and 'diyah' in accidental homicide, equating the liability of a woman and a slave to that of a free man, thereby rejecting the notion of reduced compensation for these groups. It details the heirs' option to execute both parties or accept the slave as compensation, with specific valuation rules (5,000 dirhams) ensuring fair restitution to the slave's master. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence for establishing equality in blood money regardless of gender or social status in cases of error.

en.hubeali: Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Zureys Al Kunasy who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a woman and a slave who both kill a man in error. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The error of the woman and the slave is like the deliberate. So if the guardians of the killed one like to kill both of them, they can kill both of them. So if it was such that the value of the slave is more than five thousand Dirhams, so let it be returned to the master of the slave what remains after the five thousand Dirhams; and if they like to kill the woman and take the salve, or ransom him by his master; and if the value of the slave is less than the five thousand Dirhams, so there is nothing for them except for the slave’.
